teaser.text: Antofagasta plc mines copper in Chile and sells both material that still needs refining and copper that is already ready for manufacture. It also recovers valuable by-products and runs a small freight business, so following one dollar means following rock, contracts, processing, transport and ownership.

stock.opening: Antofagasta’s weighted share price reaches 4,086.27 GBp in October 2029, a 21% total return including dividends. It hinges on Centinela’s commissioning and ramp-up from late 2027 through 2029.

paragraphs.text: By October 2029, the weighted price reaches 4,086.27 GBp, a 21% total return. The outcomes are widely dispersed: the bear case gives 1,178.50 GBp, while the bull case gives 8,336.91 GBp. Today’s price is 3,572.00 GBp. The probabilities are 30% bear, 50% base and 20% bull, reflecting Antofagasta’s volatile earnings history and the uncertainty around its expansion programme.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Antofagasta?

paragraphs.text: The bear case assumes that copper prices weaken while Los Pelambres suffers further grade, weather or labour problems. Centinela then contributes later than planned, leaving Antofagasta with high construction spending and rising debt. The share price falls to 1,394.99 GBp in October 2027 and 1,178.50 GBp by October 2029. The 30% probability reflects the 2025 production miss, the 2026 guidance cut and the speed with which EBITDA fell during the previous downturn.

The bull case requires Los Pelambres to recover, Centinela to ramp on schedule and tight concentrate supply to support copper prices. Falling project outlays then improve cash flow and reduce debt. The share price reaches 4,994.06 GBp first and 8,336.91 GBp by 2029. Its 20% probability is lower because several favorable events must occur together, while recent weather and labour disruption show the execution risk.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Antofagasta really make?

paragraphs.text: Cash from operations was $3,071.6 million in 2025. Capital spending reached $3,684.5 million, so free cash flow was negative after the main investment outflow. Lease payments and the company’s analytical stock-pay adjustment make the cash available to shareholders weaker still.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Antofagasta today?

paragraphs.text: The shares trade at 28.2x last-12-month earnings and 21.9x expected next-12-month earnings. EBITDA, earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, shows the operating engine but not the cash available to shareholders. In H1 2026, EBITDA was $2,840.5 million, while capital expenditure was $1,672.1 million. Trucks, concentrators and pipelines still require replacement and expansion, even when EBITDA margins are high. Gold and molybdenum by-products help pay the same mining bill, but free cash flow remains sensitive to construction timing and copper prices.

dividend.title: Antofagasta dividend
dividend.meta_description: Antofagasta's dividend history, cash coverage, outlook and current yield, with the risks that could change future payments.
dividend.opening: Antofagasta declared a 30.1-cent interim dividend, after dividends fell from $1.43 to $0.31 before recovering to $0.65. Antofagasta paid $395.3 million to shareholders in 2025 while free cash flow was −$719.2 million, so the dividend was not covered by that year's free cash flow.
dividend.closing: The full Antofagasta memo also answers how the business works, how it compares with rivals, how management allocates capital, and which risks could change the outcome.

blocks.heading: How much does Antofagasta pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The bear case cuts dividends to $0.55 initially and $0.46 thereafter as earnings weaken toward the 35% policy floor. The bull case rises to $1.25, $1.45 and $1.65 because stronger earnings support a similar payout ratio. The range is justified by a history in which dividends fell from $1.43 to $0.31 before recovering to $0.65.

blocks.heading: Does Antofagasta's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: Distributions continued while construction absorbed cash. In 2025 Antofagasta paid $395.3 million to shareholders and $364.8 million to minority owners. Together, it paid $1,479.3 million more than its free cash flow. The board’s recommended payout was 50.0% of 2025 earnings, showing why an earnings payout can look moderate even when construction weakens cash coverage.

Free cash flow is the cash left after operating needs and capital spending. It was $1,803.7 million in 2021, enough to fund distributions and retain $488.4 million. It then turned negative in 2022, was barely positive in 2023, and fell to −$719.2 million in 2025.

paragraphs.text: Dividends recover more slowly than EBITDA in the base case. The forecast uses $1.05 per share in October 2027 and $1.10 in October 2028, reaching $1.20 in October 2029. This keeps the payout near the 50% level achieved in 2025, while the declared 30.1-cent interim dividend supports the higher run rate.

blocks.heading: What is Antofagasta's dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: The controlling shareholder’s entities hold 60.66% of ordinary shares, which can limit outside influence without proving a minority discount. With a 1.4% dividend yield, most of the investment case depends on future cash generation.
